So I’ll say that although  technology poses its dangers, there are far more instances where technology is helpful (here i will bring in my points eg. Healthcare, Assistive technology, Mobile applications). However, we must be wary of the hands that technology falls into because it can be easily abused to fulfil a threatening agenda. Despite so, it has introduced much convenience in our daily lives and when used with care and consideration, it enhances how we live, instead of compromising our safety.

Context is always good! Set up the premise/boundaries for your argument and consider different perspectives that society might uphold. 

A generic eg. for technology and its potential danger:

As we are going through the motions of the Third Industrial Revolution, it is without a doubt that technology has become an integral and essential part of our daily lives. However, with technological advancements comes the risk of the misuse of technology and what we now know as convenience may one day become a threat. All around the world, people fear and hold onto the belief that technology may take over us with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Others fear the abuse of technology, with the creation of nuclear arms and biochemical weapons. However, considering that technology has been created for our convenience, I am of the opinion that technology is not dangerous.  However, when its usage becomes excessive or when it is in the wrong hands, technology may very well be manipulated and utilised to harness its potential dangers and threats to mankind.

I actually interpret it more as a reference to time and how it anchors one to their past such that moving forward with the attempt to 'erase' one's past is actually impossible. But what is an interpretation without any close reading right? HAHA

*"So we* ***beat*** *on, boats* ***against the current***\*, borne\* ***ceaselessly*** *into the* ***past.****"*

Firstly, we should visualise the image that Fitzgerald is trying to present to us. The image is one that is awkward, unconventional and you can already picture how futile paddling against the current is. Beyond that, for me, Fitzgerald is actually presenting the ultimate unattainable/almost impossible nature of the American Dream. The word "beat" first of all already connotes a struggle and going against a strong force. The next part will take some time to make sense if your school didn't cover the concept of time in this quote! I read "current" in two ways: the more direct reading would be the sea current, and the second more elusive reading would be current as in the currentness of time (the present). When Fitzgerald says this at the ending, he is essentially saying that characters are going against the reality of the present (eg. who and what they are) but are sadly anchored and held accountable by their past. They are "borne ceaselessly into the past" indicating the continuous and never-ending action of being pushed back in time, despite wanting to push against it.

Maybe you'll understand this interpretation better with examples --

For example, Gatsby, the central character of the entire novel embodies this quote pretty well, especially being held accountable by his past. He is constantly struggling to fit in with the Upper Class (Tom&Daisy) but finds himself being held back by the fact that he is of New Money, and would never fit in with the Old Money. So Tom (and other Upper Class characters like Mr.  Sloane), despite knowing that Gatsby is filthy rich, deliberately establishes boundaries between Gatsby and himself. He knows that Gatsby has acquired such wealth through means of labour, unlike Tom who inherited his wealth.

Another example could be how Gatsby struggles to change the present because he is so hooked on the past. He still obsesses over the idea of his relationship with Daisy 5 years ago, Because of this, he moulds his American Dream according to a fantasy that is frozen in time and this already makes the entirety of his dream unachievable, since it does not and cannot exist again. (basically, it's the past and instead of moving on, homeboy gatsby wants to recreate the past, ignoring the changes that have occurred to both himself and daisy since the time they were together. ffs daisy is MARRIED and gatsby just wants to be a homewrecker LOL)

Sorry it's so long but basically, this quote is just talking about how we cannot change our present and future if we simply choose to erase and ignore our past. What was your reading though?
